name: Nidalee
notes: Casts go one at a time behind a single busy_until: every cast reports castable_at = max(ready, now, busy_until), and a cast with a real cast time extends busy_until by that time and holds the next attack to it.

Opening: Primal Surge (Human E) is cast first for its 30-70% bonus attack speed (7 s) - Javelin Toss is deliberately held (its q_at reports INF) until Surge has been cast, so the two never race for the first slot even though both are ready at t=0.

Javelin Toss (Human Q) is then cast at the assumed maximum ~1300+ unit travel distance for the full +225% distance bonus (the sheet's DamageMulti 3.25) and to apply the Hunted mark (4 s). Since a Hunted mark resets Aspect of the Cougar's cooldown, Nidalee swaps into Cougar Form for free the instant Javelin Toss's cast ends, and stays there for the rest of the fight; cycling back to Human Form to reapply Hunted is the dossier's open question and is not modeled.

Aspect of the Cougar (R) is only the Human/Cougar transformation itself: it has no cast time and deals no damage of its own. It determines the RANK that Cougar Form's Q (Takedown), W (Pounce) and E (Swipe) scale at (per the dossier, 'Cougar Form's abilities scale based on Aspect of the Cougar's rank'), but the damage those casts deal is credited to their own native slot: Takedown under Q, Pounce under W, Swipe under E, matching the ability slot names ('Javelin Toss / Takedown' is Q, 'Bushwhack / Pounce' is W, 'Primal Surge / Swipe' is E). See 'unused' for R.

Takedown has no cast time of its own (arms the next basic attack instantly) and pays out through that attack (post-effect cooldown, attack-timer reset); its missing-health modifier reads the dummy's health at that moment, and it keeps the wiki's +30% Hunted bonus while the opening mark is still up (read as unconditional on being Hunted, not limited to a 'first cast', since Takedown's own tooltip states the bonus with no first-cast qualifier - the qualifier is on which cast gets the separate guaranteed-connect enhancement, a non-damage effect not modeled).

Pounce and Swipe do not become available until Takedown's first empowered attack has resolved, and each is only unlocked that first time at (resolution time + its own cast time): Pounce's own wiki entry gives it no cast time, but the driver keeps it serialized with the standard 0.25 s used elsewhere so it and Swipe (which does have a real 0.25 s cast time) never land in the same instant as the attack or each other; after that they simply recast on their own ~6 s cooldowns, which keeps them naturally staggered for the rest of the fight.
Bushwhack (Human W) is skipped entirely: its trap must be sprung by a unit walking into it, and the stationary dummy never does.

Takedown's critically-strikable bonus AD-as-magic-damage on the empowered attack is not modeled: the engine deals the attack's own crit damage with no hook to retype it, so only Takedown's own scaling bonus is dealt as its own source.
Mana is not modeled: Cougar-Form Q/W/E cost 0, and the two Human-Form casts (Javelin Toss, Primal Surge) each happen only once.

assumed.why: Javelin Toss's distance-based damage bonus is assumed at its maximum (a full 1300+ unit travel) rather than whatever range a real cast against the dummy would land at.

Takedown's own wiki entry gives it no cast time (distinct from the combined Q slot's dossier castTime of 0.25 s, which describes Javelin Toss); the driver uses 0 for Takedown's own arm-cast, matching its ability page.

Pounce's own wiki entry gives it no cast time, but the driver gives it the combined slot's 0.25 s so its first use and Swipe's first use do not land in the exact same instant when Cougar Form's rotation opens.

Read as an unconditional +30% to Takedown's damage whenever the struck target is Hunted (per Takedown's own tooltip), rather than limited to only the 'first cast' phrasing on Prowl's blurb, which appears to describe a separate non-damage enhancement.

unused.R: Aspect of the Cougar is only the Human/Cougar Form transformation: it has no cast time, no cooldown-relevant delay in this driver (it swaps for free off the Hunted-reset), and deals no damage itself. Its rank instead sets the scaling of Cougar Form's Q (Takedown), W (Pounce) and E (Swipe), whose damage is credited under their own native slots.
